title: Cross-region Golden Signal Normalizer and Degradation Scoring
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: golden signals (p95/p99 latency, error rate, throughput, queue depth) are currently reported independently per-region and are not normalized for workload composition (sequence length, model variant, priority). This causes noisy cross-region alerts and inconsistent circuit breaker activations. Goal: build a normalization and scoring layer that ingests regional golden signals, applies cohort-aware baselining, and emits a single cross-region degradation score used by dashboards, alerting, and adaptive load-shedding policies. Deliver a metrics pipeline, a storage schema, a scoring algorithm, and dashboard panels with drill-down into tenant/cohort-level traces.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Service computes a normalized p95/p99 latency and error rate per region and per cohort (sequence-length tier, model-variant, priority) and writes to metrics topic every 60s.
2) Cross-region degradation score produced as a single numeric metric (0-100) for each tenant and global public bucket and stored for 6 months.
3) Dashboard panels added showing: normalized heatmap by region/cohort, top 10 tenants contributing to degradation, historical score trend, and triggered circuit policy suggestions.
4) Alert rules updated to use degradation score with clear thresholds for canary and production (documented in runbook).
5) Canary rollout in us-west-2 with synthetic traffic for 48h without increase in false positives vs baseline.
6) Unit + integration tests covering baseline drift detection, EWMA smoothing, and sliding-window quantile calculations.
7) Performance: normalization pipeline end-to-end (metrics ingest -> score emit) under real-time load must stay <30s 99th percentile.
8) Documentation: design doc, runbook, and FAQ linked in Confluence and a minimal README for on-call engineers.
9) PRs merged and monitoring panels validated by SRE and PM review.
10) Rollback plan and automated kill-switch present in the deployment manifest.
11) Updated cost estimate for streaming resources included in the ticket.
12) No data schema changes that break existing dashboards until a migration plan is executed.
13) Privacy: exported metrics do not contain raw prompt/response text and comply with existing PII handling rules.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight normalization worker consumes regional golden-signal aggregates from existing metrics topic (kafka://golden-signals-aggregates), applies cohorting, computes EWMA-smoothed baselines, then writes normalized metrics and a composite degradation score to metrics_out topic.
Cohorting: initial cohorts = ['short','medium','long'] sequence-length tiers + model-variant + customer-priority. Cohort rules configurable via k/v store (consul/etcd).
Normalization strategy: use quantile-rescaling against a rolling 7-day baseline per cohort, with EWMA half-life of 12 hours to adapt to drift. Evaluate using offline replay first.
Scoring: weighted combination of normalized p99 latency, p95 latency delta, and error rate delta. Weights to be tuned by SRE and PM based on historical incidents. Score normalized to 0-100.
Backpressure integration: score thresholds map to circuit actions (observe -> throttle -> shed non-critical priority). Integrate with admission controller API (internal) via documented contract.
Trade-offs: heavier cohort granularity gives better signal but increases cardinality and cost. Start conservative cohorts and allow dynamic split on hot tenants.
Storage: store per-minute aggregates in time-series DB (existing metrics cluster), with compressed retention for 6 months. Consider rollup to hourly after 30 days.
Observability: add meta metrics for normalization worker health: processing lag, cohort cardinality, baseline stability index.
Security: metrics stream contains only numeric aggregates; confirm no token-level content flows into topic.

testing_plan: Unit tests for baseline and EWMA smoothing functions.
Integration: replay historical metrics through normalization worker and verify score correlation with known incidents (compare with incident timeline).
Canary: deploy worker in us-west-2 only, enable synthetic traffic harness (ENG-48888) with labeled tenants, validate no increase in false positives for 48h.
Chaos test: inject region failover scenario and verify degradation score spikes appropriately and triggers suggested circuit actions.
Performance: run load test at 5x current peak ingest rate to validate processing lag <30s p99.
